easy.text: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids of Giza?

options.feedback: Correct -- the pyramids of Giza were built by ancient Egyptian civilization.
Rome is famous for structures like the Colosseum, not the Giza pyramids.
Greek civilization is known for structures like the Parthenon, not the pyramids of Giza.
The Aztecs built their own pyramids in Mesoamerica, but not the ones at Giza in Egypt.

medium.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest of the three main pyramids, was built as a tomb for which pharaoh?

options.feedback: Correct -- the Great Pyramid was built for Pharaoh Khufu, also known by his Greek name, Cheops.
Tutankhamun is famous for his tomb's treasures, discovered largely intact, but he did not build the Great Pyramid.
Ramses II was a powerful pharaoh known for monuments like Abu Simbel, but not the Great Pyramid.

hard.text: During which era of ancient Egyptian history were the Giza pyramids constructed?

options.feedback: Correct -- the Giza pyramids were built during the Old Kingdom, around 2600-2500 BCE, often called the 'Age of the Pyramids.'
The Middle Kingdom came after the pyramid-building era of the Old Kingdom.
The New Kingdom, home to pharaohs like Ramses II and Tutankhamun, came over a thousand years after Giza's pyramids were built.
The Ptolemaic Period, which included Cleopatra's reign, came over two thousand years after the pyramids were built.

easy.medium: This civilization is known for hieroglyphics, mummies, and the Nile River.

medium.medium: This pharaoh is also known by the Greek version of his name, Cheops.

easy.text: The Code of Hammurabi, one of the earliest written legal codes, came from which ancient civilization?

The Code of Hammurabi originated in Mesopotamia, not China.

The Nile River valley was home to ancient Egypt, not Babylon.
Babylon was located in Mesopotamia, not the Indian subcontinent.
The Yellow River valley was a center of early Chinese civilization, not Babylon.

hard.text: Hammurabi's Code is often characterized by which legal principle, reflected in its proportional, 'eye for an eye' style punishments?

options.feedback: Correct -- lex talionis describes punishment designed to mirror the harm caused by the offense.

hard.medium: This principle is about matching the punishment to the crime, not about detention, juries, or royal authority.

topic: Julius Caesar and the Roman Empire

easy.text: Julius Caesar rose to power in which ancient civilization, which later became one of the largest empires in ancient history?

options.feedback: Correct -- Julius Caesar was a Roman general and statesman, and Rome later expanded into a vast empire.

Julius Caesar was a Roman, not a Greek, leader.

medium.text: What title did Julius Caesar hold in Rome that granted him near-absolute power, even though he was never officially called 'emperor'?

options.feedback: Correct -- Caesar was declared 'dictator perpetuo,' or dictator for life, shortly before his assassination.
Caesar did hold the consulship at times, but the title tied to his near-absolute, lifelong power was dictator.
Pharaoh was an Egyptian title -- Caesar's Roman title was dictator.

hard.text: Which of Julius Caesar's successors became the first official Roman emperor, formally founding the Roman Empire?

options.feedback: Correct -- Augustus, Caesar's adopted heir, became Rome's first emperor after the civil wars following Caesar's assassination.
Mark Antony was Caesar's ally who lost the power struggle against Augustus -- he never became emperor.
Pompey was Caesar's rival earlier in the Republic's civil wars, and died before Caesar himself -- he never became emperor.
Brutus was one of Caesar's assassins, part of a plot to preserve the Republic -- he never became emperor.

topic: Genghis Khan and the Mongol Empire

easy.text: Which Mongol leader united the Mongol tribes and founded the largest contiguous land empire in history?

options.feedback: Correct -- Genghis Khan unified the Mongol tribes and launched the conquests that built the Mongol Empire.
Kublai Khan was Genghis Khan's grandson, who later expanded the empire into China -- but Genghis Khan founded and united it.

medium.text: What was Genghis Khan's birth name before he took the title meaning 'universal ruler'?

options.feedback: Correct -- he was born Temujin and adopted the title Genghis Khan after uniting the Mongol tribes.
Kublai was his grandson's name, not his own birth name.
Ogedei was one of Genghis Khan's sons and successors, not his birth name.
Batu was Genghis Khan's grandson, who led the Golden Horde -- not Genghis Khan's own birth name.

hard.text: Which combination of factors is most credited with enabling the Mongol Empire's rapid military expansion under Genghis Khan and his successors?

options.text: Highly mobile horseback cavalry combined with an efficient long-distance relay communication system
options.feedback: Correct -- Mongol horsemen could travel and strike with remarkable speed, while the Yam relay system let commands and information move quickly across vast distances.

options.text: A large navy that dominated coastal trade routes
options.feedback: The Mongols were fundamentally a land-based cavalry power -- naval dominance was not the source of their rapid expansion.

options.text: Advanced gunpowder weapons unavailable to their opponents
options.feedback: Gunpowder weapons were not yet a major military factor during the Mongol conquests -- cavalry mobility and communication were.

options.text: Permanent, heavily fortified city walls protecting their homeland
options.feedback: The Mongols were known for offensive mobility, not for extensive fortification -- that mobility was the actual driver of their success.

easy.hard: This leader's title, adopted after unification, is now used as his most common historical name.
easy.medium: This leader united the Mongol tribes before launching conquests across Asia and into Europe.
easy.easy: This is the famous leader who united the Mongol tribes and built history's largest land empire.

easy.text: Which ancient Greek city-state is credited with developing one of the earliest forms of democracy?

options.text: There was no way for citizens to speak in the assembly

options.text: Only citizens over the age of 70 could vote
